Commons also lists Bernard Kruysen and Denis Thilliez among the complete recording’s artists. They are not credited here as soloists in the choral Agnus Dei; the organist is unidentified.

Composition rights
Public domain in jurisdictions applying an unextended life-plus-70-year term Inferred, not documented

Gabriel Fauré died in 1924. This assessment concerns the original composition, not a later edition, arrangement or this recording; it is not a worldwide rights clearance.

[3]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

Commons applies PD-EU-audio to the Erato/Frémaux recording and supplies 10 August 1962. Whether that is a session or issue date remains unresolved; its year precedes 1963. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.
